items.title: Facebook tests a two-link monthly cap for Pages.
items.para: Some Pages are limited to two link posts per month, then a prompt invites them to subscribe through Meta One.
items.tip: Check how much of your traffic depends on links. Keep them for tickets and memberships, and make matchday posts work natively.

items.title: Instagram tests 90-minute videos called Features.
items.para: Selected creators can publish podcasts, vlogs and interviews, and the test reaches select US creators from 26 October.
items.tip: Full interviews could live on Instagram. Cut Reels that link back to the long version to bring fans in.

items.title: Ads Manager now shows results for each creative.
items.para: A new Breakdown option reports individual images, videos and text variations. Carousel and collection ads are excluded.
items.tip: Learn which image or headline works for tickets or memberships, then reuse it in the next campaign.

items.title: Reddit launches a For You feed.
items.para: It recommends posts and subreddits users have not joined, next to a Following feed. The rollout is global over the coming weeks.
items.tip: Content can reach fans who don't follow you yet. Write posts that make sense without insider context.

items.title: YouTube backs microdramas with members-only episodes.
items.para: The format topped 6.5 billion views in the first half of 2026, up more than 50% year over year.
items.tip: Serial Shorts, like a season in episodes, could become a members perk. Test with one format first.
